raw_response:
I have been growing cotton here in Quzhou County for 35 years, and at 53 I know what works on my 5 mu of land. With just my wife and me at home, I do not have the labor for wheat-maize double cropping, so I keep my whole farm in cotton — it is simpler and the returns are steady.

This year I will till all 5 mu with rotary tillage before sowing, just like always. It breaks up the soil fine enough for cotton and I can do it myself with my machine. I will buy improved lumianyan28 seeds — about 3.5 jin per mu — and sow in early April. These seeds are reliable and I can get them locally.

For fertilizer, I will spread 100 jin per mu of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer as a basal dressing before sowing. That gives me enough nitrogen, phosphate, and potash to carry the crop through the season. I have tried adding extra urea topdressing in the past and did not see enough difference to bother with it on my small plot.

Irrigation is from my well. Cotton does not need flooding, so I will irrigate twice — once after sowing if the spring is dry, and again at flowering time in summer. With plastic film on the rows to keep moisture in, two times is enough.

The real work with cotton is pest control. The bollworms and aphids always come, so I will spray insecticide nine times through the season and use herbicide once. I handle the spraying myself. That keeps the damage down.

I expect to harvest around late October and get about 275 kg of seed cotton per mu. That is what I have been getting the last few years, and as long as the weather is normal it should hold.
